subject: Intermittent healthcheck flapping - suspected PMTU blackhole on private connectivity
messages:
From: Alex Singh <alex.singh@acme-corp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:05:12 -0700
Subject: Intermittent healthcheck failures to private endpoint

Marcus —

We're seeing intermittent healthcheck failures from our on-prem monitoring -> Redwood private endpoint (10.12.5.22) since ~08:40 PDT. Healthchecks are HTTP/1.1 GET to /_hc returning 502/connection reset; they succeed most of the time but we get 3-5 min flaps every ~30 minutes which impacts our HA. Attached is a traceroute and a short tcpdump capture captured from our edge NAT gateway during a failure window (healthcheck-traceroute.txt, tcpdump-acme-20270428.pcap).

Relevant details:
- Source: 198.51.100.18 (edge-nat)
- Dest: 10.12.5.22 (redwood private endpoint) over our encrypted tunnel -> TGW peering
- Tunnel: MPLS->ISP transit into region-eu (we're in us-west but route transits a partner)
- No recent config changes on our side we are aware of.

Can you advise next steps? Our SRE is available to run tests.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Intermittent healthcheck failures to private endpoint

Alex —

Thanks for the data and the pcap. I'm escalating to the private deploy/networking squad and copying the ops engineers. Initial hypotheses: path MTU blackhole (DF set + upstream firewall dropping ICMP type 3) or asymmetric routing where return traffic egresses a different ISP path and is being filtered. Both can cause intermittent resets for healthchecks which often use small windows/tcp timeouts.

Immediate asks:
- Laura/Dev: can you confirm whether our edge LB/NAT is seeing any TCP RST patterns and whether the tunnel MTU is being clamped on our side?
- Alex: could you share the edge NAT iptables config and any firewall rules that may block ICMP \"fragmentation needed\" messages? If possible, put a temporary packet capture on the ISP-facing interface for the next 30 minutes.

Temporary mitigation we can push quickly: lower the tunnel MTU to 1400 on both sides and enable a TCP MSS clamp on the NAT gateway. That usually eliminates PMTU blackholes within minutes. Let's coordinate a short maintenance window if you want us to apply the change.

I'll create a ticket and propose a rollback plan.

-marcus
Marcus Lin

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 09:22 AM Marcus Lin wrote:
> Initial hypotheses: path MTU blackhole (DF set + upstream firewall dropping ICMP type 3) or asymmetric routing where return traffic egresses a different ISP path and is being filtered.

Quick triage notes from our side (ran at 09:30-09:40):
- Security groups and NACLs for the endpoint 10.12.5.22 look fine; no deny rules matching the source.
- Edge LB (redwood-edge-uw2-01) logs: intermittent TCP handshake timeouts to 198.51.100.18 observed correlated with healthcheck gaps. No application 5xx.
- fw-logs snippet attached shows several \"ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed)\" responses from an ISP firewall IP, but those ICMP messages are consistently marked as dropped by a downstream transit ACL (fw-icmp-log-snippet.txt). That aligns with PMTU blackhole behavior.

I attached the traceroute output you provided and a short excerpt of the firewall log. Given this, lowering MTU + MSS clamp is a low-risk, high-return first step.

Proposed immediate plan:
1) Schedule a 30-min maintenance window in the next 2 hours.
2) Both sides set tunnel MTU=1400, enable MSS clamp 1360 on the NAT gateway.
3) Monitor healthchecks for 60 minutes.
4) If stable, document and make the MTU change permanent. If not, revert and escalate to ISP for PMTU ICMP fixes.

Dev, can you draft the exact iptables/iproute commands for the MSS clamp we will push?

- Laura

On Wed, Apr 28, 2027 at 10:05 AM Alex Singh wrote:
> We can do a maintenance window starting 10:30 PDT for 30 minutes.

Plan and commands (to be executed on both sides' edge NAT gateways and our tunnel endpoints):

1) Set tunnel MTU to 1400 (example for iproute2):
   ip link set dev gre0 mtu 1400
   (or adjust the MPLS/DTLS tunnel config accordingly)

2) Apply TCP MSS clamp on NAT box (iptables -- for Linux-based edge):
   iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360

3) Add temporary healthcheck monitoring rule to force 1s sampling during maintenance:
   (update monitoring policy to increase samples to ensure we catch flap quickly)

Rollback (if we see no improvement or new regressions):
- Remove the mangle rule: iptables -t mangle -D POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360
- Restore previous MTU value and re-check logs.

I'll be on the call at 10:30 to apply these on Redwood's side. Laura will coordinate cutover with Alex's team. After 60 minutes of stable healthchecks we'll promote the MTU/MSS clamp to config management.

- Dev
